prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1222; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. You already have it on the claim file.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in a parking lot at a shopping center in Sugar Land, Texas. I was pulling into a space near the entrance.
Q: What were you doing right before the impact?
A: I had just turned the wheel to back into the spot. I was going very slowly, maybe walking speed. Then a vehicle came out of the row next to me and clipped the rear quarter panel of my car.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?
A: Not really. I heard a horn and then felt the jolt. It came out fast, and I didn't have time to react.
Q: Did you notice any injuries right after the collision?
A: Not at first. I felt a little shaken up. Later that evening my right shoulder started aching, and by the next morning I could barely lift my arm above my chest.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment for the shoulder?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the following day. They took X-rays and told me to see an orthopedist for a possible rotator cuff strain. I have an appointment scheduled and I've been doing physical therapy exercises at home.
Q: Did you have any shoulder problems before the collision?
A: No, nothing that I can recall. I was lifting weights a few times a week, and I had no pain or limitations.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about how the collision happened?
A: Only that I was stopped almost completely when it happened. I feel the other driver should have been watching for cars backing into spaces.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add or correct in this statement?
A: No, I think that covers it.
Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the recorded statement.
